messages:
Alex Kim: heads-up — noticed a ~30% increase in probe-related egress and websocket connections in eu-west over the last week. cost alert flagged it this morning :grimacing:
Priya Patel: ugh. is that from streaming probes (websocket) or from higher frequency http/embedding checks?
Alex Kim: mostly streaming. we create a fresh ws per probe run from the blackbox fleet to test stall/resume behavior. each run opens ~3 sockets (control + data + health) so it adds up fast.
Jordan Lee: streaming probes are the worst for connection churn. options: 1) reduce frequency 2) reuse long-lived probe connections per runner 3) move streaming checks to a smaller canary pool in the region.
Maria Gonzalez: +1 for canary pool. We already run full-health http probes at 60s for all endpoints — keep that. Streaming tests only need to run against canaries unless we detect anomalies.
Ethan Brooks: reuse sounds ideal but requires changing how blackbox runner handles sessions. current runner is stateless by design. can we make a 'stateful runner' option?
Priya Patel: we can implement a persistent probe agent (long-lived pod) that accepts probe jobs over a control API and reuses WS connections. lower ops complexity than changing every runner. estimate: 2-3 dev-days to prototype.
Alex Kim: nice. for short-term: propose adaptive sampling algorithm: if route traffic < 5rps, probe streaming at 1/10 frequency; if >50rps keep 1x. also cap total concurrent streaming probes per-region to 50.
Jordan Lee: I like caps. Also update Prometheus scraping job to emit a metric for probe_connection_count and probe_reuse_rate so we can alert on spikes. example config we can add to infra monitoring:
```
- job_name: 'probe-agents'
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['blackbox.svc.cluster.local:9115']
  metrics_path: /metrics
  scrape_interval: 30s
```
And a blackbox exporter module for streaming smoke:
```
modules:
  streaming_smoke:
    prober: websocket
    timeout: 10s
    path: /ws/health
```
Maria Gonzalez: for embedding probes we saw noisy similarity drift early Feb. Suggest we compute a rolling baseline per-model and alert when median cosine similarity drops > 0.08 relative to baseline, but only if sample size > 100 to avoid flapping.
Ethan Brooks: good guardrails. Also add an evaluation window: require the regression to persist for 2 eval cycles (10m) before firing a Sev2.
sre-bot: Deploy job #deploy-17801 scheduled: apply change to probe-agent CRD to enable persistent-mode — CI checks passed :white_check_mark:
Alex Kim: sweet. follow-ups: Priya — can you prototype the persistent agent? Jordan — can you add the Prom metrics + grafana panels for probe health and connection churn? Maria — draft embedding similarity alert thresholds and add a k8s rollout playbook for canary-only streaming tests.
Priya Patel: on it, I'll throw a prototype branch this afternoon and ping for review. :rocket:
Jordan Lee: will add metrics and a dashboard. can we also have a cost estimate for spinning up persistent agents (GPU/no GPU?) — my guess: CPU-only micro VMs, negligible compared to ws churn but want numbers.
Maria Gonzalez: I'll draft the alert runbook and include the 2-cycle hysteresis + sampling constraints.
Alex Kim: thanks all. logging action item: add a short label to probe spans with "probe_type=stream|http|embed" so traces can be filtered. Also please tag probe-origin=canary/dedicated.
Priya Patel: noted. I'll include those labels in the prototype.
Ethan Brooks: circling back — once we have persistent agents and canary streaming-only, we should run a 48h cost A/B to quantify savings. low effort, high signal.
Alex Kim: agree. I'll create a short experiment doc after PRs land. end thread.
